content:
kai: noticed a small but consistent pattern after bringing up rerank-lite-int8: NDCG@10 slightly up, MRR@10 down. curious if this is quant effect or eval mismatch.

rebecca: numbers?

kai: fp16 -> NDCG@10=0.643 MRR@10=0.399; int8 -> NDCG@10=0.651 MRR@10=0.386. holdout=holdout-apr2026, seeds 10/11/12, topk=75.

ishaan: first check candidate pool parity and tokenizer. small normalization changes recently landed.

marie: also check priming/truncation and any post-score scaling in runtime. int8 calibrations sometimes rescale logits.

kai: propose quick ablations: (1) use prod candidates snapshot cs-2026-04-02, (2) force prod-tokenizer, (3) force prod-priming, (4) all parity. will run seeds 10..12 and report overlap/top1 shift.

ops-bot: queued eval job eval-3310007777-ablation1 for kai on runner-01.

kai: ablation1 finished: candidate overlap 98.9%, top1 changed for 1.1% queries. metrics: NDCG@10=0.649 MRR@10=0.391 p@1=0.295.

rebecca: candidate differences explain some but not all. next tokenization parity.

ops-bot: queued eval job eval-3310007777-ablation2.

kai: ablation2 (prod-tokenizer) results: NDCG@10=0.650 MRR@10=0.394 p@1=0.298. token_count_delta_fraction=0.03.

marie: priming parity should be last check.

ops-bot: queued eval job eval-3310007777-ablation3.

kai: full parity run (candidates+tokenizer+priming) -> NDCG@10=0.651 MRR@10=0.397 p@1=0.300. basically closes gap.

ishaan: conclusion: harness/candidate/tokenizer mismatches were main cause. int8 scoring distribution has minor spread changes but not primary issue.

rebecca: action items: add candidate snapshot and tokenizer version into eval metadata; add tokenization parity check to model onboard smoke tests.

kai: filed INF-4420 with artifacts and run outputs. attaching files to ticket.

(ends)
